title: The Worthing–Brighton laser test of 2 and 23 February 2019 (PIER2PIER 2, Dr John D.): their thermometer tables and trials, our transcription; the evenings' air, sea and tide

radius_enters_via.how: the 15.3 km between the sites is a distance computed on a sphere of radius R from their coordinates

verdict_rule: A laser 1 m or less above the sea seen from 1 m at 15.3 km while thermometers precise enough to see 0.1 °C per metre show no warming with height along the path, again and again, by day and by night, would favour the plane; the same beam hidden under such air would favour the globe.

inputs.checks: Each thermometer cell shows two readings ('7.5 / <7.0'); both are kept as printed.
inputs.caveats: Read off video frames: a digit can be misread where the frame is blurred; the time of the 2 February attempt is not given.

notes: Case study, not a measurement of the Earth: the operators' own readings, recomputed. Their two 'thermometers' are read from the doubled values of each cell ('7.5 / <7.0'). The time of the 2 February attempt is not given; the evening hours are kept.
license_note: The readings are facts transcribed from a public YouTube presentation (Dr John D.), cited; the API answers carry their providers' terms (ERA5 via Open-Meteo CC-BY-4.0, IEM, IOC SLSMF, NOAA OISST public domain).
